Subject: Initial: on-prem zoning + attachment map for Acme pilot

Hi Jonas / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, Acme's site team has sketched a first-pass zoning map for their colo racks and the proposed attachment points for the Redwood on-prem runtime. I attached a draw.io export (site-zones-v3.drawio.png) and a CSV that lists VLANs, expected BGP peers, and allowed egress destinations.

High-level asks from Acme:
- Validate that the proposed control-plane endpoints (listed in the CSV) will not traverse tenant-exposed BGP sessions.
- Confirm recommended NAT/egress model for sampler telemetry (short-lived metrics vs. long-lived traces).
- Call out any service adjacency or firewall rules that would prevent KV cache replication between the on-prem runtime and Redwood's regional relay.

We want to get a short internal audit before sending this to Acme's network security team. Can you review and flag anything obvious? Alex from Acme is on the CC and available for clarifying questions.

Attachments: site-zones-v3.drawio.png, attachment-zone-matrix.csv

—Paul

Thanks Paul — got the files and summary. Looping in Kim, Marissa, and Mateo for a quick architecture audit.

Quick notes from me (please expand):
- Control plane endpoints look like three regional relays (us-west/us-east); need to confirm that the proposal pins control-plane traffic to dedicated management VLANs and does not hairpin through tenant routes.
- KV cache replication must use mutual TLS to the relay; confirm that edge's ACLs permit outbound mTLS to our relay IP set (will provide IP list).
- Telemetry egress: prefer a push-proxy pattern (short-lived collector) to avoid long-lived outbound streams from tenant networks.

Kim — can you validate the BGP peer details in the CSV and call out any missing route filters?
Mateo — can you review suggested firewall rules and whether the proposed HA pair for the on-prem proxy satisfies our failover SLOs?

If we can get edits in the next 48 hours I'll put together a short readout for Acme's security team.

—Jonas

Subject: Re: Initial: on-prem zoning + attachment map for Acme pilot — audit notes

Thanks — I had a look through the CSV and the draw.io export. I attached a cleaned diagram (redwood-onprem-reference-v1.pdf) with inline callouts. Summary of findings / changes I recommend: 

1) Control-plane isolation
- The CSV shows control-plane IPs in the same VLAN as tenant management. Recommend: move control-plane endpoints to a dedicated management VLAN (Mgmt-VLAN-100) with explicit route-filtering to prevent transit to tenant subnets.
- NOTE: If the site team intends to use existing OOB (out-of-band) management, we should document the fallthrough behavior when OOB is unavailable.

2) BGP peers and route filters
- Missing inbound prefix-lists on Acme's edge: add a deny for 10.0.0.0/8 and 172.16.0.0/12 if those ranges are used internally for tenants. I flagged the specific rows in attachment-zone-matrix.csv.
- If the site's BGP is using AS-PATH prepends for traffic steering, ensure we have clear community tags so our regional relays can prefer healthy paths.

3) KV cache replication and TLS
- Confirmed: Vaulted certificates are OK, but the site must allow outbound TCP 443/7843 to the relay IPs. If the site blocks 7843, fall back to 443 with SNI-based routing.

4) Telemetry egress pattern
- Recommend a push-proxy (short lived) that tunnels telemetry to our ingest cluster in us-west. This keeps long-lived egress streams off tenant-facing infra.

5) Firewall rules and HA
- Suggested firewall rule examples are in the attached PDF. For HA pair, ensure floating VIPs are in the same subnet as the proxy so health-checks don't cross tenant ACLs.

I attached redwood-onprem-reference-v1.pdf and updated the CSV rows with comments. I'll add specific ACL examples in a follow-up if you want.

Attachments: redwood-onprem-reference-v1.pdf

—Kim
Kimberly Park

Subject: RE: Initial: on-prem zoning + attachment map for Acme pilot — audit readout & action list

Paul / Alex — thank you for the drawings and for the patience while we reviewed. Below is a concise readout for Acme's network/security teams, plus action items and owners. We'll include the annotated diagrams and the CSV with inline comments on the drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1SiteZoningReview

Readout (tl;dr)
- Control-plane endpoints must be moved to a dedicated management VLAN (Mgmt-VLAN-100). This prevents accidental transit via tenant routes and satisfies our control/data separation requirement.
- BGP inbound prefix-filters and community tagging required (see CSV).
- KV cache replication OK assuming outbound mTLS (TCP 443/7843). If 7843 is blocked, Redwood will negotiate a port/proxy fallback over 443.
- Telemetry: implement short-lived push-proxy pattern; do not allow long-lived telemetry streams from tenant-facing subnets.
- Firewall: follow the example rules in redwood-onprem-reference-v1.pdf; HA requires VIPs to remain in the proxy subnet.

Action items and owners
- Paul (EdgeOps): update draw.io source with Mgmt-VLAN assignment and resubmit by Wed 03/03. (Attachment: site-zones-v3.drawio.png)
- Alex (Acme): confirm whether site allows outbound ports 7843/443 to Redwood relays (reply here by 03/04).
- Jonas (Redwood Deployments): provide relay IP list and SNI endpoint details by 03/02.
- Kim (Network Security): produce concrete ACL examples and a port-fallback statement (deliverable: ACL examples doc) by 03/04.
- Mateo (Ops): validate HA VIP behavior in the proxy subnet and confirm failover test plan (deliverable: failover checklist) by 03/05.

If we get the updated diagrams and port confirmation on the timeline above, we'll prepare a one-page evidence packet for Acme's security review. Sending the annotated PDF and the CSV in case you want to start with those.

Attachments referenced: redwood-onprem-reference-v1.pdf, attachment-zone-matrix.csv
Related: JIRA INFRA-4832 (preflight).

—Marissa
